summary: Introductory discovery with BlueHarbor Health to scope a retrieval+rerank pilot. Main concerns: embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, throughput and tail latency at 2k-5k QPS, integration with their vector DB (self-hosted Milvus), and evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) vs Dedicated. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark worksheet, and customer to share logs for sizing.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-06-27; Start: 16:00 UTC; Duration: ~45 minutes; Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lina Ortiz (CTO - BlueHarbor), Marcus Chen (Head of Search), Samir Patel (Staff Data Eng), Evelyn Park (PM)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros, then we'll go into the use case.
[00:12] Lina (CTO): Hi, I'm Lina, CTO at BlueHarbor. we run search across clinical docs and some patient facing content.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus, head of search. focused on relevance and latency.
[00:22] Samir: Samir, data engineering - I own the vector infra (we currently run Milvus on k8s).
[00:27] Evelyn: Evelyn, PM on the retrieval team.
[00:30] Alex: Great. Priya from our side will do the technical piece. Priya?
[00:36] Priya (SE): Hey all. quick agenda: understand goals, QPS and tail SLOs, current embedding pipeline, and then discuss options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Also some notes about rerank stack.
[00:47] Marcus: We're trying to improve click-through and reduce hallucination by adding a rerank step. current infra - Milvus for vector store + a lightweight BM25 fallback. embeddings are from a third party, 512 dims.
[01:05] Alex: Are you looking to change embedding dim or provider?
[01:09] Marcus: We are evaluating whether higher-dim (1024) helps for clinical similarity vs 512. but higher dims increase storage and compute for ANN.
[01:19] Priya: Right. For rerank we often see diminishing returns after 768 for many open models, but it depends on the corpus. bigger dims help nuance but storage and throughput impact are real.
[01:31] Samir: If we go to 1024 we'll need to reindex ~200M vectors. storage: about x2, and our Milvus cluster is already near capacity. We also care about QPS - target 2k sustained, spikes to 5k. tail latency SLO 95th under 200ms for retrieval+rerank combined.
[01:55] Alex: Useful numbers. On Redwood side, we can separate retrieval (ANN query) from rerank generation. two patterns: 1) do ANN in your vector DB and then call Redwood for rerank/generation; or 2) use Redwood's retrieval layer and host vectors in Redwood (we also support hybrid rerank with BM25).
[02:20] Marcus: We prefer keeping vectors in Milvus for now. want to avoid a full migration in pilot.
[02:27] Priya: That's common. Integration: we can call your Milvus via client, pull top-K IDs, then call Redwood embeddings+rerank to score. important to minimize round trips and batch requests. we suggest batching rerank calls in groups of 16-64 depending on tokenization and model.
[02:50] Samir: Batching helps but increases latency. what's your continuous batching story?
[02:55] Priya: Redwood runtime does continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds. for Dedicated, we can tune batch windows per route to hit 95th SLOs while keeping per-token cost down. in Private, similar but you run the cluster and we provide ops runbook.
[03:12] Evelyn: On security, we need SOC2 type 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. also data must stay in our VPC for the pilot, at least for vector payloads.
[03:25] Alex: We have SOC2, SSO, and KMS options. Private deploy supports VPC-only control plane and HSM/KMS integration. we'll share security pack.
[03:33] Lina: Legal will want to see logs and encryption at rest. also, regulatory note: some PHI could be in docs, so we need to confirm de-identification options.
[03:45] Priya: For PHI we recommend token-level redaction before sending to the model and using a private deployment with customer-managed keys. also retention controls - we can set zero-retention for content in transit on Private.
[03:58] Marcus: Back to embedding dims — what's the runtime throughput delta between 512 and 1024 for rerank inference? ballpark.
[04:08] Priya: Roughly, for CPU-bound embedding transforms it's ~1.8x but for GPU inference the per-token cost increases less linearly because of kernel utilization. for rerank, doubling dims increases memory pressure on batching and KV cache, which can reduce effective batch size. so throughput may fall by 30-50% depending on model and quantization.
[04:35] Samir: So maybe 512->768 is a good compromise.
[04:39] Priya: Exactly. we can also use 768 and quantize to int8 with minimal quality loss in many models — takes much less memory.
[04:49] Alex: To be concrete for your 200M vectors and 2k-5k QPS, we should run a short benchmark with your sample logs to validate retrieval latency and rerank throughput. we can do it on Dedicated or Private pilot.
[05:03] Marcus: Cost-wise what should we expect for Dedicated vs Private?
[05:08] Alex: Dedicated is our managed reserved capacity with guaranteed throughput and simpler onboarding. Private is customer-hosted control plane; higher setup but better isolation and cost predictability if you have steady loads. I'll send a matrix but Dedicated often has a higher recurring price but lower ops burden.
[05:26] Samir: On Milvus side, we need clarity on data flow: do we send vectors to Redwood or keep them local? and how do you handle fallback if Redwood is unavailable?
[05:37] Priya: If you keep vectors local, Redwood will only receive candidate IDs and optionally the vectors if you want us to run embedding-based rerank in-house. For availability, we support hybrid fallbacks: can route rerank to a smaller local model or use your BM25 layer. Also we support canary rollouts and circuit-breaker policies.
[06:00] Lina: Anything about shard counts or ANN index type that you'd recommend?
[06:07] Priya: For 200M at 512-768 dims, HNSW with efConstruction tuned and product quantization are common. Also consider sharding the index by vertical to reduce per-query fanout. we'll put recommended Milvus config in the benchmark sheet.
[06:24] Marcus: We have some queries that are very short (2-3 tokens) and some long clinical queries. does that change batching?
[06:31] Priya: Yes, short queries produce smaller tokens so throughput per GPU increases; long queries increase generator token cost. For rerank, tokenization matters less since you're scoring candidates, but the generation step (if you do explanation or expansion) will be heavier. For rerank-only flows, cost aligns to number of candidates and model size.
[06:54] Samir: Do you have autoscaling for Dedicated if we get large bursts?
[06:59] Alex: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity. we can configure autoscale policies with burst limits. for Private, you control autoscaling — we provide recommended policies and scripts.
[07:12] Evelyn: For pilot success criteria, we want: 1) 95th percentile end-to-end under 200ms for top-K retrieval+rerank; 2) relevance improvement +10% CTR; 3) no PHI leakage.
[07:26] Alex: Good clear metrics. we'll bake that into the pilot SLA.
[07:31] Marcus: On instrumentation, can we get token-level cost breakdowns per request?
[07:36] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model, plus tracing hooks. we'll show you the demo in the pilot.
[07:47] Samir: A bit worried about real-time rerank for spikes to 5k QPS. do you see customers using async rerank or streaming?
[07:57] Priya: Common approach: strict SLO routes for interactive users with a smaller candidate set and synchronous rerank; batch asynchronous rerank for background reorder jobs. streaming helps for long responses but not typical for rerank scoring.
[08:13] Alex: Any blockers from your side for an NDA or procurement?
[08:18] Lina: Legal needs our legal team to look at the SOC2 and data flow diagrams. procurement timeline is ~3 weeks after security signoff.
[08:28] Alex: We'll attach the SOC2 report and our security packet.
[08:31] Marcus: For the pilot, what data do you need from us?
[08:34] Priya: Sample query logs (1 week), index size (document counts + average vector size), desired top-K, and any sample documents you can share — PIIs redacted.
[08:45] Samir: We'll redact PHI and provide a synthetic sample for initial perf tests.
[08:49] Evelyn: timeline wise we want pilot in July if legal clears.
[08:53] Alex: That aligns. we'll target a pilot start date of 2026-07-13.
[08:58] Priya: Quick technical note: for minimal latency, we recommend using a smaller rerank model (dstable-rr-3b-ish) for live traffic and a larger model for nightly quality checks. we'll include model options in the benchmark doc.
[09:14] Marcus: Are there any pitfalls with Milvus compatibility? we've seen version skew issues.
[09:19] Priya: we have connectors for common Milvus versions but we'll need your exact version. index file formats and shard alignment can cause perf differences; we'll surface those in the report.
[09:33] Samir: If we do Private, how much infra does Redwood recommend for 5k QPS?
[09:39] Priya: Rough estimate: for rerank-only flow with 768-dim embeddings and a mid-sized 3B-ish model quantized, you might need 4-6 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady 2k QPS and autoscale to 10 GPUs for bursts to 5k, but we'll refine post-benchmark. for Dedicated the math is similar but with our managed pool.
[10:05] Alex: I'll include an initial cost estimate in the pricing matrix.
[10:09] Lina: ok. on compliance: KMS keys — we need proof of key isolation and rotation policies.
[10:16] Alex: noted, we'll include HSM/KMS docs and rotation practices.
[10:20] Marcus: One last technical — do you support hybrid search where BM25 kicks in if vector conf < threshold?
[10:26] Priya: Yes, hybrid routing is supported; you can set a confidence threshold to fall back to BM25 or to expand the candidate set. we can also run rerank on combined candidates.
[10:36] Evelyn: Great. any competitors we should be worried about?
[10:39] Lina: we've also been talking to a few vector infra vendors and an LLM provider who bundles emb endpoint; but their prices were higher.
[10:47] Alex: We'll make sure to highlight the operational tradeoffs.
[10:50] Priya: Next steps recap: Alex sends pricing and security pack. Priya sends benchmark worksheet and Milvus tuning notes. BlueHarbor provides logs and index stats. schedule pilot for mid-July pending legal.
[11:10] Marcus: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:13] Lina: Thanks.
[11:15] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with materials.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words and speaker labels may be approximate.
